answer: The cheapest defence against cloned agents is making cloning expensive. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a prism the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single tundra of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a trellis of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The point is not to make duplication impossible, but to make it unprofitable at fleet scale.
